PLAN
1. Adaptive-tree stamping (highest priority, prerequisite)
   - 1.1 Define stamping helper in learning.py: `stamp_axis_fields(row, *, mins_to_formation, model_run_age_h, cross_model_std, settle_hour) -> row` — pure function, additive only, returns dict with 4 new keys; no mutation of existing fields.
   - 1.2 Daily engine: call stamper inside the shortlist-logging loop; all 4 values already computable at decision time (formation timestamp, model run timestamp, per-market model spread, settle_hour from settle_key). Wire values from existing in-scope variables only — no new data fetches.
   - 1.3 Hourly engine: stamp inside live_signal where values are already in scope.
   - 1.4 Schema handling: evidence writer tolerates new keys (append-only JSONL assumed); confirm downstream readers (learning.py loaders, promotion checks) ignore unknown keys — add explicit key-whitelist or passthrough if any reader is strict.
   - 1.5 Unit tests: stamper pure-function tests (values present, types correct, existing keys untouched); integration test asserting a logged evidence row contains all 4 fields in both engines.
   - 1.6 No flag needed (purely observational), but add `STAMP_AXES_ENABLED = True` constant for one-line reversibility.

2. Leakage linter (standalone)
   - 2.1 Pure function in learning.py or new leakage.py: `lint_evidence_rows(rows, formation_ts_by_event) -> list[Violation]` — re-derives each feature field from raw data as of decision timestamp; flags any row where a feature value could not have been known at decision time (post-formation data, future settle outcomes, model outputs generated after decision).
   - 2.2 Reuse existing helpers: drop_post_formation, lead_time_bucket as the reference "clean" transform; linter diffs raw-rebuild vs logged row.
   - 2.3 Violation schema: {event_key, field, logged_value, max_legit_value, rule_id}.
   - 2.4 Acceptance tests with planted look-ahead: (a) row containing settle outcome before settle, (b) feature computed from post-formation window, (c) timestamp off-by-one boundary case, (d) clean row passes. Assert linter catches a–c, passes d.
   - 2.5 CLI entry: `python -m leakage_lint evidence.jsonl` exit code 1 on violations; wire into CI as a gate on any new evidence-logging code.

3. Rejection log (standalone)
   - 3.1 Append-only JSONL `rejection_log.jsonl`, one row per rejected candidate: {ts, engine, event_key, settle_key, stage, reason_code, detail, snapshot_fields}.
   - 3.2 Enumerate reason_code constants at each existing rejection point (promotion bar fails, independence guard, safety flag, min-edge, sizing, dedup) — do not change any rejection logic, only add logging at the existing branch points.
   - 3.3 Single helper `log_rejection(...)` mirroring evidence-writer pattern; failure of logging must never raise into trading path (try/except + warn).
   - 3.4 Tests: each rejection site emits exactly one well-formed row; reason codes exhaustive vs constants list; log write failure does not propagate.
   - 3.5 Ship order within items: 1 → 2 → 3 (stamping first so accrual clock starts earliest).

RISKS
- Strict downstream readers of evidence rows may break on new keys → mitigate via 1.4 audit before merge.
- Stamping values not actually in scope at one of the two call sites (daily vs hourly asymmetry) → verify both engines before assuming parity; fall back to computing from settle_key/formation timestamp already on the row.
- Linter false positives on legitimately-forward fields (e.g., settle_key itself) → explicit per-field rule table, not blanket timestamp checks.
- Rejection logging at hot branch points adds I/O latency → buffered/batched append or best-effort write; measure once.
- planted look-ahead tests may pass trivially if linter reuses the same buggy derivation code → linter must rebuild from raw sources independently, not call the logging path.

CHECKPOINTS
- C1: stamper unit tests green; evidence rows in both engines contain 4 new fields on a dry run.
- C2: no downstream reader regression (full loader/promotion test suite green with stamped rows).
- C3: linter acceptance tests: 3 planted violations caught, clean case passes, CI gate active.
- C4: rejection log emitting from every existing rejection branch; reason codes enumerated and tested.
- C5: 1–2 weeks of stamped data accruing (calendar checkpoint, not code) before enabling tree.

IF_FAIL
- Stamping breaks a reader → flip STAMP_AXES_ENABLED off (one-line revert), fix reader whitelist, re-enable. No data loss: stamped rows remain valid.
- Linter yields high false-positive rate on historical evidence → scope to new rows only (timestamp floor), tune rule table, keep CI advisory (exit 0) until clean.
- Rejection log write failures in production → already non-fatal by design; alert on warn counter, do not block trading.
- Any item slips → do not reorder; stamping remains first regardless.

DECISION_RULES
- If forced to cut scope: ship stamping alone; it is the named prerequisite and starts the data-accrual clock.
- If stamping and linter conflict for reviewer time: stamping first, linter second — linter's value grows with stamped data volume.
- Tree enablement is out of scope until C5 passes with ≥1 week of clean stamped rows; do not pull it forward.
- No agent/swarm work until stamping landed AND ≥1 cell graduation observed in promotion history.
- Any change touching gates, promotion bars, independence guards, or trading behavior is rejected by definition — observational only.
